title: BUILDING MACHINE TRANSLATION SYSTEMS FOR THE NEXT THOUSAND LANGUAGES

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative error analysis and human evaluation of machine translation outputs across low-resource languages, specifically examining how models mistranslate dialects into related high-resource languages (e.g., Kalaallisut into Danish, Sanskrit into Hindi) and how they magnify training data noise by substituting dialects with offensive or toxic slang (e.g., translating Nigerian Pidgin into offensive US slang).

Evaluating the disparity in model performance and language coverage between high-resource European languages and historically under-served/long-tail languages (e.g., indigenous languages of the Americas, African languages) using character-level metrics (ChrF) and round-trip translation evaluation.
